markup:
A **home battery backup system typically costs $8,000–$20,000 installed** for a system that can keep essential appliances running during a power outage.

If you want to power your entire house, including air conditioning, the cost can reach **$20,000–$40,000 or more**.

## Home battery backup cost breakdown

| System size | Typical installed cost | What it can power |
|---|---:|---|
| 5 kWh | $4,000–$8,000 | Refrigerator, Wi-Fi, lights |
| 10–15 kWh | $9,000–$16,000 | Essential household circuits |
| 20–30 kWh | $16,000–$30,000 | Most household appliances |
| 40+ kWh | $30,000–$50,000+ | Larger homes, longer outages |

These are approximate U.S. prices before incentives, assuming a permanently installed system.

## Example: Tesla Powerwall 3

    <title size="lg">$13,000–$16,500</title>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Typical California installed price, 2026</text>
    - 13.5 kWh battery capacity
    - Automatic backup during outages
    - Works with or without solar panels
    - 10-year warranty
  </box>
</row>

California's average installed battery cost is currently around **$1,030 per kWh**. <Cite refs={["turn143119search0","turn143119search8"]}/>

One important detail: the federal 30% homeowner battery tax credit ended for systems placed in service after December 31, 2025. Some state and utility incentives remain. <Cite refs={["turn143119search2","turn143119search5"]}/>
